name: Zoetis
description: Zoetis is the animal-health company spun out of Pfizer, selling medicines, vaccines and diagnostics for pets (about 70 percent of 2025 revenue) and livestock (about 29 percent). The customer is a veterinarian, who buys from Zoetis and sells to the pet owner, or a livestock producer; in some markets Zoetis also sells pet products through retail pharmacies and e-commerce. Two product lines carry the company: Simparica/Simparica Trio (parasite control for dogs) was about 16 percent of 2025 revenue and Apoquel (itch and dermatitis in dogs) about 12 percent; the top five product lines were about 42 percent. It reports two geographic segments, US ($5.1B) and International ($4.3B). In 2026 the pet business has weakened: US companion animal revenue fell 11 percent in Q2 2026 on softer demand, competition in dermatology and parasiticides, generic competition to Cerenia and Convenia, and lower Librela sales.

gics.note: SEC SIC code 2834 (Pharmaceutical Preparations). Zoetis sells only to animals: pet drugs, vaccines and diagnostics (70% of 2025 revenue) and livestock products (29%), so it is priced by veterinarians and pet owners, not by insurers or Medicare like human pharma.

hq.note: 10 Sylvan Way, Parsippany, NJ 07054 (SEC EDGAR business address). Incorporated in Delaware in July 2012; previously a business unit of Pfizer (FY2025 10-K).

employees.note: About 14,500 employees worldwide (about 6,800 in the US), including about 1,700 in global R&D; FY2025 10-K

businessLines.shareBasis: Share of revenue = 5,097 / 9,467 total revenue (the rest is International 4,254 and contract manufacturing and human health 116). Share of profit = 3,438 / 5,702 total reportable segment earnings.
businessLines.how: Veterinary clinics buy the medicines, vaccines and diagnostics and sell them on to pet owners; livestock products go to veterinarians and producers. Revenue follows volume sold through veterinarians and price; the Q2 2026 10-Q attributes the recent decline to softer end-market demand, competition and price sensitivity.
